title: Jimi Hendrix invites Paul McCartney to a New York recording session | 1969
content:
Jimi Hendrix sent a telegram to Apple’s London HQ on 21 October 1969, inviting Paul McCartney to take part in a recording session in New York City.

Hendrix was recording with trumpet player Miles Davis and drummer Tony Williams. The telegram read:

PAUL MCCARTNEY APPLE RECORDS 3 SAVILE ROW LONDON/
ENGLANDW1

WE ARE RECORDING AND LP TOGETHER THIS WEEKEND IN NEWYORK STOP HOW ABOUT COMING IN TO PLAY BASS STOP CALL ALWAN DOUGLAS 212-5812212

PEACE JIMI HENDRIX MILES DAVIS TONY WILLIAMS

The telegram, sent via producer Alan Douglas, arrived at Apple the following day. Unfortunately, McCartney was unavailable, having taken Linda and their two daughters to High Park Farm in Scotland.

Apple’s managing director Peter Brown sent a response declining the invitation.

Ref. cable received from Hendrix Davies and Williams.

Paul McCartney away from London on holiday not expected to return for two weeks.

PETER BROWN

Hendrix’s planned album with Davis never came to fruition. Although they jammed together on occasion, their schedules and financial issues meant that they were unable to come together, with Davis reportedly wanting $50,000 upfront to attend the sessions.
